question: Is X-linked intellectual disability, Siderius type inherited ?
references: This condition is inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern. The gene associated with this condition is located on the X chromosome, which is one of the two sex chromosomes. In males (who have only one X chromosome), one altered copy of the gene in each cell is sufficient to cause the condition. In females (who have two X chromosomes), a mutation would have to occur in both copies of the gene to cause the disorder. Because it is unlikely that females will have two altered copies of this gene, males are affected by X-linked recessive disorders much more frequently than females. X-linked intellectual disability, Siderius type, also known as X-linked intellectual disability, Siderius type, is a rare genetic disorder caused by mutations in the PAK3 gene. This condition is inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern.

In X-linked recessive inheritance, the mutated gene is located on the X chromosome. Females have two X chromosomes (XX), while males have one X and one Y chromosome (XY). 

In the case of X-linked recessive disorders, males are more frequently affected than females because they have only one X chromosome. If a male inherits the mutated gene on his single X chromosome, he will express the condition. Females, on the other hand, have a second X chromosome that can compensate for the mutated gene, reducing the likelihood of expressing the condition. However, females can still be carriers of the mutated gene and may pass it to their offspring.

So, to answer your question, X-linked intellectual disability, Siderius type is indeed inherited.
